chunks: Someone asked him (peace be upon him) to define faith for him.

So he said (peace be upon him): Come to me tomorrow so that I may inform you in the hearing of the people, so that if you forget my statement, someone else will preserve it for you, for speech is like a dart; this one catches it and that one misses it.

key_terms.أَسْمَاعِ النَّاسِ: In the hearing of the people

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali define faith and ensure its preservation?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delays the definition of faith to deliver it publicly, emphasizing the communal preservation of knowledge against the fragility of individual memory. This metaphor of speech as a dart highlights the selective nature of human reception, a key theme in Shia epistemology regarding the transmission of divine truth. The delay also suggests that the definition of Iman is profound enough to require a public forum for full comprehension and collective witness.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 266. Someone asked Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, to define religion for him,

so he said: Come to me tomorrow so that I enlighten you in the presence of all the people, so that if you forget what I say others might retain it, because an utterance is like a fluttering prey which may be grappled with by someone but missed by others.
